PHASE_1.question: Does the band deficit track signal-MC support loss / sparsity under thinning?
PHASE_1.VERDICT: REFUTED BEFORE RUNNING, on evidence already on record. NOT RUN, and it should not be run.

reason_1_regressor_is_constant_by_constr.note: Thinning is i.i.d. and kinematics-independent, so support loss is uniform IN SHARE. Same defect that retired the OI-126 tiebreak, whose discriminating variable was exp(-1).

reason_2_the_amplifier_is_mislocated.STATED_PRECISELY_BECAUSE_THE_TWO_COMPARI: A sparsity amplifier predicts the effect at the LOW TAIL, and there the band is the DENSER set (min 42 vs 1, q25 912.5 vs 421.25). At the MEDIAN the band is the sparser set (2382 vs 5505.5). Only the low tail is the mechanism's prediction, and the mechanism does not get it. Quoting the median comparison would reverse the conclusion.

PHASE_1.what_this_does_NOT_establish: It does not exonerate the signal stream. Occupancy is a support statistic; signal MC enters through a TRAINED NETWORK, which can respond non-uniformly to a uniform perturbation. What is refuted is the SPARSITY AMPLIFIER, which was the only local amplifier the campaign had named.
